messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Jacobian warning for missing-data model
parts:
Hi folks,

Below is a model for multivariate data with missing observations. I thought I was doing the proper thing by treating the missing data as parameters and then creating a new matrix to contain both the non-missing data and the missing-data-as-parameters values, but I get the Jacobian warning (http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#parser-warnings), so presumably I'm not thinking about this correctly or there's another step I need to do that I'm missing. Thoughts?



  data {

    # N: number of cases
    int<lower=1> N ;

    #: K: number of outcome variables
    int K ;

    # Y: matrix of outcomes for each case & variable
    matrix[N,K] Y ;

    # n_missing: number of instances of missing data
    int n_missing ;

    # indices_of_missing: matrix of the row and column indices of missing data
    int indices_of_missing[n_missing,2] ;

  }
  parameters {

    # means: vector of population-level means per variable
    vector[K] means ;

    # sds: vector of population-level sds per variable
    vector<lower=0>[K] sds ;

    # cor: population-level correlations amongst variables
    corr_matrix[K] cor ;

    # imputed: vector of imputed values for missing observations
    vector[n_missing] imputed ;

  }
  transformed parameters{

    # cov: covariance matrix (derived from cor & sds)
    matrix[K,K] cov ;

    # Y_with_imputed: matrix of data and imputed values
    matrix[N,K] Y_with_imputed ;

    # add imputed values to non-missing observations
    Y_with_imputed = Y ;
    for(i in 1:n_missing){
      Y_with_imputed[indices_of_missing[i][1],indices_of_missing[i][2]] = imputed[i] ;
    }

    #compute covariance matrix from cor & sds
    cov = quad_form_diag(cor,sds) ;

  }
  model {

    #priors on population parameters; presumes data has been scale()ed
    means ~ normal(0,1) ;
    sds ~ lognormal(0,1) ;
    cor ~ lkj_corr(1) ;

    #assert sampling of case-level outcomes on each variable given
    #  multivariate normal population
    for(s in 1:N){
      Y_with_imputed[s,] ~ multi_normal(means,cov) ;
    }

  }

messages.subject: Re: Jacobian warning for missing-data model
parts: Oh, I think that Ben's answer here (https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/mEGf1RFBlcU/B0lySgHoZPsJ) implies that one can ignore the Jacobian warning in cases like this where there is a transformed parameter on the left-hand-side of a tilde, but that TP is merely the combination of data and parameters, and therefore a safe linear transformation of the parameters.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Jacobian warning for missing-data model
parts:
This is fine — technically there is a Jacobian, but it’s equal to 1 so
the log Jacobian vanishes.  The problem with the warning is that by
statically evaluating the code we can’t distinguish between trivial 
Jacobians like this and nontrivial Jacobians that actually matter.
